sections.title: 1. Scope
sections.summary: This standard applies to all employees, contractors and visitors at the Pune and Chennai plants.
sections.text: This standard applies to all employees, contractors and visitors at the Pune and Chennai plants. Where a local rule is stricter, the stricter rule applies. Version 5 replaces Version 4 (2024); the main changes are listed in section 9.

sections.title: 2.2 Visitors
sections.summary: Visitors must be escorted at all times in production areas and wear safety shoes, safety glasses and a visitor vest.
sections.text: Visitors must be escorted at all times in production areas and wear safety shoes, safety glasses and a visitor vest. Visitors may not enter the heat treatment area or the paint shop. Visitors who are not wearing safety shoes may only use the marked visitor walkway.

sections.title: 2.3 Contractors
sections.summary: Contractors must complete the safety induction (45 minutes) before starting work and receive a contractor badge valid for 12 months.
sections.text: Contractors must complete the safety induction (45 minutes) before starting work and receive a contractor badge valid for 12 months. Contractors working at height or on electrical equipment also need a work permit (section 5) for each job.

sections.title: 3.1 What to report
sections.summary: Report every injury, near miss, fire, spill of more than 5 liters of oil or chemicals, and any damage to a machine guard.
sections.text: Report every injury, near miss, fire, spill of more than 5 liters of oil or chemicals, and any damage to a machine guard.

sections.title: 3.2 Deadlines
sections.summary: Event Report to Deadline Serious injury (hospital treatment, fracture, amputation) Plant manager and EHS head by phone Immediately, within 1 hour Lost time injury EHS head Within 4 hours First aid injury Shift supervisor
sections.text: Event Report to Deadline Serious injury (hospital treatment, fracture, amputation) Plant manager and EHS head by phone Immediately, within 1 hour Lost-time injury EHS head Within 4 hours First-aid injury Shift supervisor Before the end of the shift Near miss Shift supervisor, through the HSE app Within 24 hours Fire (any size) Fire control room (extension 333) Immediately Chemical spill above 5 liters EHS head Within 2 hours A written investigation report must be completed within 7 calendar days for lost-time and serious injuries, and within 14 days for near misses with a high potential severity.

sections.title: 3.3 Night shift
sections.summary: On the night shift (22:00 06:00) the shift supervisor acts for the plant manager for the first report.
sections.text: On the night shift (22:00 - 06:00) the shift supervisor acts for the plant manager for the first report. The plant manager must still be informed by 08:00.

sections.title: 4. Lockout / tagout (LOTO)
sections.text: 1. Inform the area supervisor and the machine operators. 2. Switch off the equipment using the normal stop. 3. Isolate all energy sources: electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, stored mechanical energy. 4. Apply your personal padlock and tag to every isolation point. Every person working on the equipment applies their own lock. 5. Release stored energy and wait the discharge time stated in the machine manual. 6. Verify zero energy: try to start the machine and measure voltage. 7. After the work, remove only your own lock. A lock left by someone who has left the site may only be removed by the area manager after a documented check, with the EHS head informed.

sections.title: 5. Work permits
sections.summary: A work permit signed by the area supervisor and EHS is required for: hot work (welding, grinding, cutting outside the grinding bay), work at height above 1.8 meters, confined space entry, and electrical work on live equi
sections.text: A work permit signed by the area supervisor and EHS is required for: hot work (welding, grinding, cutting outside the grinding bay), work at height above 1.8 meters, confined space entry, and electrical work on live equipment. Permits are valid for one shift. Hot work requires a fire watch for 30 minutes after the work ends. Electrical work on live equipment above 50 V additionally needs the approval of the plant electrical engineer.

sections.title: 6. Forklifts
sections.summary: Only employees holding a valid Helix forklift license (renewed every 3 years) may drive forklifts.
sections.text: Only employees holding a valid Helix forklift license (renewed every 3 years) may drive forklifts. Speed limit 10 km/h in the warehouse and 5 km/h in production halls. Pedestrians have priority on marked walkways. Contractors may not drive Helix forklifts.

sections.title: 7. Working hours and fatigue
sections.summary: No one may work more than 12 hours in a shift or more than 60 hours in a week, including overtime.
sections.text: No one may work more than 12 hours in a shift or more than 60 hours in a week, including overtime. Between two shifts there must be a rest period of at least 11 hours. Exceptions need the written approval of the plant manager and may not be used for more than 2 consecutive weeks.

sections.title: 9. Changes from Version 4
sections.summary: The near miss deadline is now 24 hours (was 48 hours).
sections.text: The near-miss deadline is now 24 hours (was 48 hours). Hearing protection is required in the machining hall above 85 dB(A) (was 90 dB(A)). Contractor badges are valid for 12 months (were 6 months). The maximum working week is 60 hours (was 64 hours).
